Title: Search API Pricing Compared 2026

URL Source: https://awesomeagents.ai/pricing/search-api-pricing/

Published Time: 2026-04-19T00:00:00Z

Markdown Content:
**TL;DR**

*   Cheapest per-query at scale: Serper at $0.30-$1.00/1k queries depending on plan, with a 2,500-query free tier per month
*   Best value for agent workloads: Brave Search API Data for AI tier - fresh web results plus structured data extraction at $0-$5/mo for low volume, $5/mo for 2k queries/mo on the Pro plan
*   Tavily is purpose-built for AI agents with relevance filtering and answer extraction included; $0.008/query on the Research plan
*   Exa neural/semantic search starts at $0.001/result but costs compound fast with content retrieval add-ons
*   SerpAPI is accurate but expensive at $50/5k queries ($10/1k) - use it for Google result fidelity, not volume
*   Bing Web Search API: Microsoft announced end-of-life for March 2025. Do not build new pipelines on it
*   Jina Reader and Firecrawl price content extraction separately from search - budget for both if your agent needs to read page content

## The Bottom Line

Search is the most underpriced line item in most agent cost models. Teams obsess over LLM token costs and ignore that at 1M agent queries per month, search API bills routinely exceed model bills. The spread across providers is extreme: from $0.30/1k queries at the cheap end to $10/1k at the premium end - a 33x range for roughly equivalent web results.

The complication is that "search" means different things depending on your pipeline. A basic SERP provider returns 10 blue links. An agent-specific provider like Tavily returns ranked, relevance-filtered snippets with an answer synthesis layer. Exa returns semantically matched results from a neural index. Jina Reader and Firecrawl handle the content extraction step - what happens after you get a URL back. These are not directly comparable products, so I've organized pricing around what you're actually building.

For benchmark data on search quality and agent task completion rates, see the [AI agent benchmarks leaderboard](https://awesomeagents.ai/leaderboards/agentic-ai-benchmarks-leaderboard/). For RAG pipeline architecture guidance, see [best RAG tools 2026](https://awesomeagents.ai/tools/best-ai-rag-tools-2026/).

## Ranked Pricing Table

Sorted by effective cost per 1,000 queries on a mid-volume plan. Where providers charge per request with response count multipliers (e.g., 10 results per query), I've normalized to per-query cost. Prices verified April 19, 2026.

| Provider | Per 1k Queries | Freshness | Free Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Serper | $0.30-$1.00 | Real-time Google | 2,500/mo | Cheapest Google SERP by a wide margin |
| Brave (Data for AI) | $0-$5/mo flat | Near-real-time | 2k/mo free | Subscription tiers, not per-query |
| ValueSerp | $1.50 | Real-time Google | 100 calls/mo | Budget Google SERP alternative |
| Exa (neural) | $1.00-$5.00 | Indexed (hours-days) | 1k/mo | + content retrieval extra |
| Jina Reader | $2.00 | Live page fetch | 1M tokens/mo | Content extraction, not search |
| Tavily (Research) | $8.00 | Real-time web | 1k/mo | Agent-optimized, includes snippets |
| SerpAPI | $10.00 | Real-time Google | 100/mo | Most search engines, highest fidelity |
| Perplexity Sonar | $8.00-$15.00 | Real-time web | $5 credit | LLM-generated answers, not raw SERP |
| You.com Smart API | ~$10.00 | Real-time web | 60/day | AI answer API with citations |
| Firecrawl | $15.00-$19.00 | Live crawl | 500 credits/mo | Crawl + scrape, not pure search |

_Brave Search pricing is subscription-based, not per-query. Per-1k equivalent shown for the Data for AI $5/mo plan at 2k queries/month = $2.50/1k. Free tier gives 2k/mo at $0._

## Cost at Scale

Raw dollar cost at 10k, 100k, and 1M queries per month. Where providers use subscription tiers, I've taken the most cost-effective matching tier.

| Provider | 10k queries/mo | 100k queries/mo | 1M queries/mo |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Serper (Dev plan) | $3 | $27 | $270 |
| Serper (Pro plan) | $7.50 | $75 | $750 |
| Brave Data for AI | ~$25 | ~$100 | ~$400 (enterprise) |
| ValueSerp | $15 | $150 | ~$1,200 |
| Exa (basic) | $10-$50 | $100-$500 | $1,000-$5,000 |
| Tavily (Research) | $80 | $800 | $8,000 |
| SerpAPI | $100 | $500 | ~$4,000 |
| Perplexity Sonar | $80-$150 | $800-$1,500 | $8,000-$15,000 |
| You.com Smart | ~$100 | ~$600 | Contact sales |
| Jina Reader | $20 | $200 | ~$2,000 |
| Firecrawl | $150-$190 | ~$1,500 | Contact sales |

The Serper vs. Tavily gap is the most striking: at 1M queries, Serper costs roughly $270-$750 vs. Tavily's $8,000. The difference is what you're paying for. Serper gives you raw Google SERP results. Tavily gives you ranked, filtered, agent-ready content. Whether that 10x cost differential is worth it depends on how much post-processing your pipeline does in-house.

* * *

## Per-Provider Breakdown

### Brave Search API

**Pricing:** Subscription tiers. Free: 2,000 queries/month. Basic: $5/month for 20,000 queries. Starter: $20/month for 100,000 queries. Standard: $40/month for 500,000 queries. Premium: custom pricing.

**What you get:** Brave's Data for AI plan is specifically built for LLM grounding and RAG. Results include rich structured data - infoboxes, FAQs, news results, location data, and discussions from Reddit/forums. The freshness tier is configurable: you can request results indexed within 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days. Brave runs its own independent web crawler rather than licensing Google data, which matters for agents that need to avoid a single point of dependency.

**Best fit:** Agent pipelines needing structured grounding data at predictable monthly costs. The $5/month tier handles 20k queries - more than sufficient for a small production agent. The flat-rate model makes budget forecasting easy.

**Gotchas:** Coverage is narrower than Google-backed providers. Freshness is configurable but near-real-time, not instant. The free tier's 2k/month cap runs out fast in development if your agent is chatty. Enterprise pricing is contact-sales, so modeling costs above 500k/month requires a call.

Source: [Brave Search API](https://brave.com/search/api/)

* * *

### Tavily

**Pricing:** Free: 1,000 searches/month. Research plan: pay-as-you-go at $0.008/search ($8/1k). Custom enterprise contracts above ~1M/month.

**What you get:** Tavily is the most agent-native search API in this comparison. It was built from day one for LangChain, LlamaIndex, and similar frameworks - the SDK ships with direct integrations. A single Tavily query returns pre-ranked results with relevance scores, extracted content snippets, and an optional AI-generated answer. That answer synthesis step means you might be able to skip a separate LLM call for simple factual questions. Tavily also includes search depth settings: `basic` (faster, cheaper) vs. `advanced` (slower, more sources scraped).

**Best fit:** Agent loops that query search frequently and need results pre-processed for LLM consumption. If your agent is doing multi-step research, the relevance filtering reduces noise significantly compared to raw SERP results.

**Gotchas:** $8/1k is expensive if you hit the search step frequently. At 100k searches/month, Tavily costs $800 - compare that to $75 with Serper Pro. If your pipeline can handle raw SERP results with your own post-processing, Tavily's value proposition weakens at scale. The `advanced` search depth costs more and is not clearly documented in per-request pricing.

Source: [Tavily](https://tavily.com/)

* * *

### Exa

**Pricing:** Free: 1,000 searches/month. Paid plans start at $0.001/result (where each search returns up to 10 results, so $0.01/search at maximum results). Content retrieval (fetching full page text) is an additional $0.001/page. Custom pricing at scale.

**What you get:** Exa is semantically different from every other provider here. Instead of keyword matching against a traditional web index, Exa uses neural search - meaning you can send natural language queries and get back semantically similar documents rather than keyword-matched pages. This works well for research tasks where you're looking for documents like "academic papers on attention mechanisms" rather than querying with exact keyword phrases. Exa indexes the web but their index is optimized for clean, structured content - academic papers, documentation, news, blogs - rather than the long tail of the web.

**Best fit:** Research agents, document retrieval pipelines, and RAG systems where semantic similarity matters more than freshness. Not the right tool for "what happened today in AI news."

**Gotchas:** The per-result pricing looks cheap ($0.001/result) but compounds quickly. A search returning 10 results plus content extraction for each result = $0.01 (search) + $0.01 (10 page fetches) = $0.02 per query. That's $20/1k queries - 20x the headline. Model the full pipeline cost, not just the search query price. Freshness
